10.1c — 3-Button Jam: Core Loop & Self-Playtest

A toy becomes a game the moment it can start cleanly, escalate tension, end in a clear win or loss, and restart in one button press. Once your loop closes today, you put on your cruelest critic hat and run a five-part Self-Playtest to expose edge cases before friends ever touch the keyboard.

In the Code + Editor: Close the Loop & Add Escalation (~30 min) ~30 min
  1. Track Score or Progress On Screen: wire a simple TextMeshProUGUI readout for score, timer, or health so players never guess how close they are to winning or losing.
  2. Build One Clear Escalation Ramp: avoid building five static stages when one dynamic ramp creates real tension — speed up spawns over time, shrink a timer using Mathf.Max(), or introduce a second hazard shape once score passes a threshold.
  3. Wire Instant Restart Inside the 3 Buttons: when Game Over or Victory triggers, display a short message (e.g., "Press J to Play Again") calling SceneManager.LoadScene() so restarting takes half a second with zero mouse clicking.
Structured Self-Playtest: Try to Break Your Own Game (~25 min) ~25 min

Developers usually play gently along the "intended path." Force yourself through these five adversarial tests and write down every failure honestly:

Self-TestWhat You Intentionally DoPass / What Broke?
1. Idle TestTouch ZERO keys for 15 seconds after starting.
2. Spam TestMash all 3 buttons as fast as possible simultaneously.
3. Edge / Hold TestHold movement/charge keys permanently against screen edges or boundaries.
4. 3-Button AuditPlay 3 full runs (Start → Die/Win → Retry) WITHOUT touching any 4th key or mouse outside your 3 buttons.
5. Escalation CurvePlay seriously for 60 seconds: is the start boring or instantly impossible, and does the difficulty ramp noticeably?

Socratic: Catching Your Own Blind Spots

  1. Which of the five self-tests broke or embarrassed your game most today (idle survival, button mashing, escaping off-screen, or restart state leaking across runs)?
  2. Compare playing your own game cleanly versus running the Spam and Idle tests: why do edge-case tests catch bugs that normal playthroughs hide for days?
  3. Name the single fix you will ship BEFORE friend playtesting next class so testers actually spend time reacting to your design rather than getting trapped in a bug.

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Complete a full start → challenge → escalation → win/loss → instant retry loop
  • Keep score/health/goal visible on a TextMeshProUGUI HUD
  • Run all five self-playtest stress tests and fix soft-locks or off-screen escapes
  • Commit and push your self-tested loop cleanly
